name: Ram
overview: Ram is a male biblical figure recognized primarily as an ancestor of Barachel. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded, his mention in Scripture connects him to the genealogy referenced in the book of Job. There are no further notes elaborating on his life or role beyond this ancestral connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Ram is a proper name meaning 'high' or 'exalted.' This meaning reflects a sense of elevation or prominence, though the name was not given directly by God. The single recorded instance of this name appears in Job 32:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ram as an ancestor of Barachel, establishing a genealogical link between the two. Beyond this ancestral relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Ram's significance in Scripture lies in his role as an ancestor of Barachel, situating him within the genealogical framework mentioned in Job. Although not a prominent figure with detailed narratives or deeds, his mention contributes to the biblical understanding of lineage and heritage. This connection underscores the continuity of God's people across generations as recorded in the Old Testament.
